key_insight: EAServe makes the multimodal Encode stage the control point for a three-stage EPD serving pipeline, coordinating downstream admission, prefill placement, and GPU sharing to fix resource imbalance.
engineering_relevance: For MLLM serving, this provides a practical way to raise throughput and GPU utilization under SLO constraints by jointly managing pipeline flow and co-located execution.
method: Runtime: adaptive micro-batching plus rate-controlled partial offload from Encode to a co-resident Prefill worker.
Runtime: dynamic SM partitioning for predictable GPU co-location.
HAS config layer: profiles stage capacity, prunes unbalanced GPU allocations, then uses TPE-based Bayesian optimization over GPU allocation, encode batch size, and offload ratio.
evidence_signal: On three MLLM architectures spanning image, video, and audio, the system achieved up to 4.3x better goodput than NVIDIA Dynamo and 1.7x over vLLM under the same SLOs.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate per-stage capacity profiling and careful GPU partitioning/offload tuning, which may be harder to generalize across hardware and model variants.
paper_title: EAServe: Encode-Aware Disaggregated Serving for Multimodal Large Language Models
